workstream: ribo_audit part 2: the biologically correct locus for each unresolved ribosomal run
prior_exposure: From part 1 and its addendum the author has seen: every TOK / WCP / EMB diagram of the part-1 sample, the census labels of TOK, L4b, L4b+, L1, and the L4b gap table (junction marker pairs, strand flips, recurrence). No WA L4b or Z L4b+ case has been opened. The literature list below was compiled from the papers cited, not from our flanks; genes seen in part-1 flanks enter only where a cited paper lists them (SecY, cytidylate kinase, TruB/Cbf5, ndk, infB, enolase do; EMC3_TMCO1, DNA_primase_lrg, Peptidase_M48, Prefoldin, TrmB do not).

S10_spc_core.genes: uL22, uS3, uL29, uS17, uL14, uL24, uL5, uS14, uS8, uL6, uL18, uS5, uL30, uL15 (14-gene core in Asgard, non-Asgard archaea and bacteria) + archaeal S4e, L32e, L19e, RNase P protein component 1 (RNP1) + secY at the distal end; uS19 precedes uL22
S10_spc_core.sources: W09 (spc: L14-L24-S4e-L5-S14-S8-L6-L32e-L19e-L18-S5-L30-L15-secY in 92% of 26 genomes), T23 (core + RNP1, S4e, L32e, L19e; SUI1 homolog in the cluster figures), A89 (secY distal in the M. vannielii spc unit)

S10_small.genes: uS10, uL3, uL4, uL23, uL2; uL3-uL4-uL23 always co-occur; uS10 often elsewhere
S10_small.variation: occurs separately from the 14-gene core in Asgard and many non-Asgard archaea (T23); contiguous with it in the bacterial S10 operon

alpha_L13.genes: uS13, uS4, uS11, rpoD; frequently followed by L18e, uL13, uS9, rpoN (rpoK in some); one transcription unit incl. eno in Haloarcula marismortui
alpha_L13.variation: split into S13-S4-S11 and rpoD-L18e-L13-S9 in Asgard; S13-S4-S11 found with L34e-L14e-Cbf5 near the S10-spc cluster in five Asgard genomes

L34e_group.genes: L34e, cytidylate kinase (cmk), L14e; Cbf5 (TruB-family pseudouridine synthase) in Asgard

L7ae_group.genes: L7ae, S28e, L24e, ndk, infB (IF-2), S6e, eIF2-gamma, Utp24

L30e_str.genes: rpoH, rpoB (split), rpoA (split), L30e, nusA, uS12, uS7, EF-2, EF-1alpha

L11_group.genes: uL11, uL1, uL10, P1 (L12 equivalent); secE, spt5 nearby

established_cluster_content.other_separate: S24e-S27ae with rpoE1/rpoE2; pNP-S15-S3ae; S19e-COG2118-L39e-L31e-eIF6-LXa; L21e-rpoF; L37ae-rpoP; L44e-S27e-eIF2alpha; S6e-eIF2gamma; L15e (W09, T23)
established_cluster_content.variation_known: gene order and content vary (CV05); spc split onto opposite strands in Methanopyrus (W09); L24-S4e separated in Pyrobaculum (W09); clusters dispersed in Nanoarchaeum equitans (Wa03, W09); alpha split in Asgard (T23); uL10/L16 outside the S10 operon in most archaea (W09)
established_cluster_content.operon_spacing: within-operon distances peak at short values including overlaps of 1 and 4 nt, borders are flat (S00); distance models are genome-specific, co-expression drops near 20 bp in Halobacterium and 50 bp in H. pylori, opposite-strand pairs are a different class (P05)

annotation_mapping_rules.R_ribosomal_protein: Pfam hit named '^ribosom(al)?_' (the run marker) OR KOfam KO whose KEGG name (DB source 'kegg') contains 'ribosomal protein'

N_literature_member.rpoD_N_K: KO K03047 / K03058 / K03055 or Pfam RNA_pol_L / RNA_pol_N / RNA_pol_Rpb6
N_literature_member.eno: KO K01689 or Pfam Enolase_N / Enolase_C
N_literature_member.cbf5_truB: KO K03177 / K11130 or Pfam TruB_N / TruB_C_2 / DKCLD
N_literature_member.EF2: Pfam architecture with EFG_C or EFG_IV and GTP_EFTU

annotation_mapping_rules.X_other: every other gene; genes with neither Pfam nor KO are X and flagged 'unannotated'
annotation_mapping_rules.naming: observed domains and these literature names only; no other functional names

evidence_rules.b_operon_structure: adjacent genes are LINKED if on the same strand and intergenic distance d = start(next) - end(prev) - 1 <= 150 nt, or <= 500 nt when both genes are members (R or N; functional class supports the link as in S00). A strand change is never linked.
evidence_rules.component: maximal chain of linked genes; cut where >= 3 consecutive X genes occur; leading and trailing X genes trimmed; qualifies with >= 2 member genes including >= 1 R. X genes inside a qualifying component are co-transcribed inserts and belong to the locus.
evidence_rules.accurate_description_of_a_run: units = qualifying components containing >= 1 marked run gene, plus each marked run gene outside every qualifying component as a singleton unit. ONE locus iff one unit; that component is C. Multiple loci otherwise: the targets are the qualifying components with >= 3 member genes.
evidence_rules.c_inheritance: for each decisive junction (cut, glue or edge), gene identities = KO, else Pfam architecture, else none; counts of other genomes of the own lineage group ($RD/lineagefree/groups/emb_hom_average_t0.75) and of other groups holding the two identities <= 2 positions apart, and of group genomes holding both identities at all. Reported beside each case; used for the inherited / single-genome flag, not for the verdict.
evidence_rules.d_data: gene-call anomaly within 1 gene of the decisive point: adjacent same-strand genes sharing a KO or a Pfam domain (split ORF), a member longer than 2x or shorter than 0.5x the median of its KO or top marker (fusion / fragment); contig end inside or at the edge of C
evidence_rules.excluded_from_verdict: family-token bonds, recurrence counts, cohesion and every statistic of the methods (reported only)

verdicts.procedure: for each run unresolved by an output (standing rule): (7) no qualifying unit, or coordinates missing -> cannot tell; else (6) a data anomaly within 1 gene of the decisive point -> data problem; else (2) multiple units -> the benchmark glues them; else (one locus C): (3) the output resolves C (best locus by overlap with C, >= 80% of C and >= 80% inside C); (5) some other output locus resolves C; (1) best covers < 80% of C -> the output split C (the cut junctions are reported with strand, distance, classes, inheritance); (4) coverage met, precision against C < 0.8 -> the output extends beyond C, should have stopped at C's edges
verdicts.flags: unannotated gene at the decisive junction; junction single-genome in its group (no other group genome with the same adjacency although >= 1 holds both identities)
verdicts.correct_output_for_1_and_4: C itself (gene ids and positions given)
verdicts.review: every case diagram read; a verdict is changed only for a demonstrated computation error, fixed in code for all cases; disagreements recorded

answers_plan.A: all 1,686 runs: right iff every target (C, or each component with >= 3 members) is resolved by its largest-overlap locus at 80 / 80; ceiling = runs with >= 1 target
answers_plan.B: on the frozen primary (WA L4b) and L4b, with each output's own bonds (s_k = 0 = unbonded): (i) bridge an unbonded junction between two loci when the two flanking gene families lie in one locus of the same output in >= 3 other lineage groups; (ii) bridge when >= 1 other genome of the own group holds the two families <= 3 positions apart. Report: verdict-1 cases repaired (C resolved after merging loci across firing junctions); fires over all junctions where one locus ends and the next starts on the same contig in DPANN; merges of two different curated instances (package gold: DefenseFinder, TXSScan, CRISPRCasTyper, instances with >= 2 member genes) against merges inside one instance
answers_plan.C: scoring corrections justified by (a)-(d): target = accurate loci (members and co-transcribed inserts included, units split at strand changes / non-member gaps, singleton marked genes dropped); resolved counts of all four outputs; chance = random windows (5 per run, same starts as the part-1 controls) with length equal to the target length
answers_plan.D: configuration features of the frozen primary that the verdicts contradict, with counts
